resolved.note: Akien on this class: 'i have no idea.' NB he ratified it 2026-07-17 by signature gate ('I think we're done, yes. CC++') and it already carries an OPEN RULING awaiting him. Owner-does-not-recognize-it is its own finding, carried out of this item.
resolved.cc_read_of_the_consequence: CC's read of the consequence, NOT ruled: this does not merely fill three empty cells — it relocates the workflow from the CLASS to the INSTANCE. cairn/tools/base/transitions.py::_registered_workflow refuses any version a class does not define, and _conform requires the node's path to MATCH the class-registered path exactly (free_summons aside). Under this ruling both are validating against the wrong owner: there is no class-level path for a ticketer-composed workflow to conform to. code-seam and skill still carry workflow_versions v1/v2, so the change is not a no-op for them either. What the class plausibly still owns is the CONSTRAINTS (which summonses are gates that may not be skipped) — that preserves the original why (a string cannot quietly skip PROVEME) while letting the ticketer compose the path. That reconciliation is a design detail for the corpus, not another question for Akien; it is carried into the consequence ticket, not settled here.
